# Example-
# And another example-

> At the onset of the monsoon, ten times the square root of a flock of swans flew away to <term>Manasa</term> <gloss>a sacred lake in the Himalayas</gloss>. One-eighth of the flock flew up from the water's edge and went to a forest of land-lilies. Oh young girl, three pairs of swans were seen playing with great passion in the water beautified by young lotus stalks. Tell me the total number of the flock. 3.

**Prose Order:** Oh girl! At the arrival of the clouds, ten times the square root of a flock of swans went to <term>Manasa</term> lake. One-eighth part flew from the shore and reached a forest of land-lilies. Three pairs of swans were seen eagerly engaged in playful sport in water adorned with tender lotus fibers. Then, tell the total count of the entire flock. 3.

**Meaning:** Oh beloved, sixteen years of age! There was a group of swans. Among them, when the rainy season arrived, ten times the square root went to <term>Manasaro-vara</term> lake. One-eighth part of the flock flew from the edge of the water into a forest of land-lilies. Six swans <note>three pairs</note> were seen playing very affectionately in water glowing with tender lotus stalks. Tell me, how many swans were in that group? 3.

**Mathematical Setup:** Multiplier of the square root is 10. The fraction is <gloss>1/8</gloss>. The visible quantity is <gloss>6</gloss>. As the rule states "when increased or decreased by fractions," here we divide the visible quantity and the square root multiplier by one minus the fraction <gloss>7/8</gloss>. The resulting visible quantity is <gloss>48/7</gloss>. The square root multiplier becomes <gloss>80/7</gloss>. Half of the multiplier is <gloss>40/7</gloss>. Its square <gloss>1600/49</gloss> added <note>to the product of the visible quantity and the denominator</note> results in <gloss>1936/49</gloss>. The square root of this is <gloss>44/7</gloss>. Adding half the multiplier <gloss>40/7</gloss> and squaring the result gives the total flock of swans: 144.

**Explanation:** According to the rule mentioned in the second verse, the eighth part <gloss>1/8</gloss> was subtracted from one <note>the whole</note>, so <gloss>1/1 - 1/8</gloss> = <gloss>7/8</gloss>. This was divided into the visible quantity 6, resulting in <gloss>6/1 / 7/8</gloss> = <gloss>6/1 × 8/7</gloss> = <gloss>48/7</gloss>. Thus, <gloss>48/7</gloss> became the adjusted visible quantity. Similarly, the square root multiplier 10 was divided by the remaining fraction <gloss>7/8</gloss>, so <gloss>10/1 / 7/8</gloss> = <gloss>10/1 × 8/7</gloss> = <gloss>80/7</gloss>. This became the adjusted multiplier. Now, treating <gloss>48/7</gloss> as the visible quantity and <gloss>80/7</gloss> as the multiplier, the operation was performed according to the method in the previous verse. Specifically, half of the multiplier <gloss>40/7</gloss> was taken. Its square was <gloss>1600/49</gloss>. This was added to the visible quantity <gloss>48/7</gloss>...

<summary>This page presents a poetic mathematical problem involving a flock of swans to demonstrate the solution of quadratic equations. It provides the verse, a prose explanation, and a step by step calculation resulting in the number 144.</summary>
